Ritzey Therapeutics Launches With $112.5 Million
The biotech startup, founded by Intra-Cellular Therapies' former CEO, debuts with a Series A round and a DYRK1A inhibitor candidate.
Updated on Nov. 23, 2026 in Biotech
Ritzey Therapeutics launched with $112.5 million in Series A funding led by Vida Ventures and acquired an oral DYRK1A inhibitor candidate from France's Perha Pharmaceuticals. AI Illustration. Upload story photo >
Ritzey Therapeutics has launched with $112.5 million from a Series A round led by Vida Ventures, backed by EcoR1 Capital, Fidelity Management & Research, and Perceptive Advisors. The company also acquired a clinical-stage, oral, once-daily DYRK1A inhibitor candidate from France's Perha Pharmaceuticals.
Why it matters
The launch brings a new drug developer into the DYRK1A inhibitor space, with the funding intended to advance the pipeline led by the acquired candidate. The company is led by Sharon Mates, Ph.D., founder and former CEO of Intra-Cellular Therapies.
The company's lead asset is a clinical-stage, oral, once-daily DYRK1A inhibitor acquired from Perha Pharmaceuticals. The $112.5 million Series A round is the disclosed capital base, and the source does not specify the drug's dosing data or trial sample sizes.
The players
Ritzey Therapeutics
A newly launched biotech company focused on developing DYRK1A inhibitors for conditions including Down syndrome and diabetes.
Intra-Cellular Therapies
A U.S. drug developer whose schizophrenia and bipolar medication Caplyta was among its products before Johnson & Johnson acquired it in 2025.
Johnson & Johnson
A multinational healthcare company that acquired Intra-Cellular Therapies in 2025 for $14.6 billion.
Perha Pharmaceuticals
A French pharmaceutical company that sold a clinical-stage DYRK1A inhibitor candidate to Ritzey Therapeutics.
The details
Ritzey Therapeutics was launched by Sharon Mates, Ph.D., alongside fellow members of Intra-Cellular Therapies' senior management team. The company will use the cash to advance its DYRK1A inhibitor pipeline, starting with the candidate acquired from Perha Pharmaceuticals.
Timeline
2025: Johnson & Johnson acquired Intra-Cellular Therapies for $14.6 billion.
November 23, 2026: Ritzey Therapeutics debuted with its $112.5 million Series A funding.
The Tech Race
The launch follows Johnson & Johnson's 2025 $14.6 billion acquisition of Intra-Cellular Therapies, whose former CEO Sharon Mates now leads Ritzey. The move shows former leaders of a major acquired biotech reinvesting in new DYRK1A-focused pipelines.
The mid-stage trial in Down syndrome patients would test whether the drug affects pancreatic beta-cell function and tau pathology. Patients with diabetes could eventually see the candidate evaluated for Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes if the trials succeed.
The takeaway
Overexpression of DYRK1A is linked to insulin insufficiency and cognitive dysfunction, so a candidate that targets it could address more than one condition if later studies confirm the preclinical findings. Readers should watch for trial results from the planned Down syndrome and diabetes studies.

articles.title: Avicena raises $100M to link AI chips with microLEDs instead of lasers
articles.snippet: Avicena raises $100M to link AI chips with microLEDs instead of lasers The Next Web
articles.text:
Avicena’s connectorised LightBundle microLED link, shown in September 2026
Credit: Avicena
Avicena, a Sunnyvale startup that links AI chips with tiny LEDs instead of lasers, has raised more than $100M in Series C funding. It also has a new chief executive. Kevin Pope succeeds Marco Chisari and will lead the company as it brings its first product to market next year.
InterVest led the round, Avicena announced on Tuesday. Other investors include Tiger Global, Cerberus Capital Management, SK hynix Ventures, Samsung Catalyst Fund and AMD Ventures. Prosperity7 Ventures, Mitsubishi Chemical’s Diamond Edge Ventures and Hitachi Ventures also took part. InterVest director John Dongwoo Ha joins Avicena’s board.
“AI infrastructure needs a new approach to moving data between accelerators, memory, and switches,” Pope said.
Light instead of copper
AI systems move ever more data between accelerators, memory and switches. Copper links face limits on reach, density and energy use, Avicena says. Memory bandwidth and capacity also increasingly hold systems back. SK hynix, one of the investors, has said the memory shortage will last until 2030.
Avicena’s LightBundle platform uses dense arrays of microLEDs and silicon photodetectors linked by multicore fibre. Rather than pushing a few channels very fast, it spreads data across many slower ones. That, the company says, cuts the need for data-rate conversion and complex signal processing.
Because it needs no lasers, the platform can sit close to compute and memory chips. Avicena pitches it for links inside and between chip packages, and across accelerator systems. By contrast, Photon Bridge raised $10M last month to build lasers for AI data centres.
From evaluation kits to a product
Avicena began shipping 1Tbps LightBundle evaluation kits in August. In September, it announced a version with connectors for the ECOC 2026 optics conference. It is meant to make assembly, testing and servicing easier.
The money will go on hiring, product development and engineering, Pope said. Two of the chipmakers behind the round see a role for the technology in memory.
“Energy-efficient optical interconnects are becoming increasingly important to next-generation memory architectures,” said SK hynix Ventures’ Rene Do.
SK hynix Ventures said it hopes to work with Avicena on future memory interconnects. Energy and data movement limit the AI build-out, said Samsung Catalyst Fund’s David Goldschmidt. AMD Ventures’ Patrick Rundell said moving data between compute, memory and networking chips is becoming critical.
Earlier this month, Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum , the Nvidia-backed optical component maker, in an all-stock deal.

articles.snippet: China Physical AI Roundup: Simplexity Robotics Raises $100M Pre-A, Plus X Square Model, OYMotion and AgiBot Deployment AI Insider
articles.text:
Physical AI · Humanoids
China Physical AI Roundup: Simplexity Robotics Raises $100M Pre-A, Plus X Square Model, OYMotion and AgiBot Deployment
By Greg Bock · 24 November 2026 · 3 min read
AI Insider
Insider Brief
China’s physical AI sector saw new funding, robot technology releases and industrial deployments, alongside government efforts to develop national standards for embodied-intelligence data.
Simplexity Robotics raised $100 million at a $1.6 billion valuation and unveiled its iX wheeled humanoid, while OYMotion secured several hundred million yuan to expand its dexterous hand and robot training technology.
X Square Robot reported a 55.1% zero-shot success rate for its WALL-OSS-1.0 model across 312 real-robot tasks, while AgiBot began trial operations of its Genie G2 robots on a semiconductor testing line in Shanghai.
China ‘s physical AI industry continues to expand on several fronts, with fresh investment, advances in robotic intelligence and growing activity in industrial settings. This week’s developments also highlight specialized hardware, training data and emerging standards as companies work to move robots beyond demonstrations and into commercial use. Here’s a look at the latest developments.
Simplexity Robotics
Simplexity Robotics has raised $100 million in a pre-Series A round led by Ant Group at a $1.6 billion post-money valuation, Ifeng reported , citing chairman and co-founder Wang Kai. Wang made the comments in a Bloomberg interview and said Ant also joined as a strategic investor. TechNode , also citing Bloomberg, said existing investors Tencent, HSG and Lanchi Ventures participated as well and that the company was founded by former Li Auto executives.
Wang listed the company’s current backers as Vision Plus Capital, HSG, Lanchi Ventures, Tencent, Alibaba, Legend Capital, CAS Star and Gaorong Ventures, according to Ifeng. He said Lanchi, Tencent, Legend Capital and HSG have each invested in three or more rounds.
Simplexity also unveiled iX, its second humanoid and a wheeled robot that prepares and delivers drinks, fetches items and guides visitors, Ifeng said. Early customers include Korean robotics startup RLWRLD, Tsinghua University and forklift maker Hangcha Group. Simplexity has already put a warehouse sorting line into operation with Hangcha.
X Square Robot
X Square Robot introduced WALL-OSS-1.0, a vision-language-action foundation model for robots, the Shenzhen company announced . It reported a 55.1% zero-shot success rate across 312 real-robot tasks chosen by evaluators, with no task-specific training. On ManipArena, a real-world benchmark of 15 tabletop tasks, the model scored 1,101 out of 1,500 points without task-specific fine-tuning, 70.8% higher than a fine-tuned π0.5 baseline, according to the company.
X Square said a compact Nano version of the model ran 18 robots on one Nvidia Blackwell GPU in a tested configuration. It also said a WALL-OSS-1.0-based parcel-sorting policy for an unnamed logistics customer kept more than 90% of its original-site speed and success rate when moved across sites. The company said it will open-source the model’s weights soon.
OYMotion
OYMotion , a Shanghai maker of dexterous robot hands and muscle-signal technology, has closed a Series D of several hundred million yuan, 36Kr reported in an exclusive, citing the company. Harbinger Secures More Than $100 Million in Debt Financing from Erebor Bank and Pinegrove Venture Partners to Support Production Ramp and Future Growth
News provided by
Harbinger
Nov 24, 2026, 11:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
The combined capital was provided through term loan, revolving debt and convertible note financings to support Harbinger's next stage of growth
GARDEN GROVE, Calif. , Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Harbinger , an American industrial technology platform company, today announced it has closed financing agreements totaling more than $100 million with Erebor Bank , co-founded by Palmer Luckey , and Pinegrove Venture Partners , which is sponsored by Brookfield Asset Management and HRTG Partners. The complementary financing structures include senior debt provided by Erebor and a separate convertible note from Pinegrove.
Continue Reading
Harbinger has secured more than $100 million in financing from Erebor Bank and Pinegrove Venture Partners to accelerate production and support its growing commercial vehicle business.
The transactions mark an important step in Harbinger's evolution from an electric vehicle manufacturer to a broader industrial technology platform company reinventing the critical systems the world depends on across mobility, power, defense, autonomy and components. Harbinger develops advanced electrification technologies, including all-electric and hybrid medium-duty vehicle platforms, battery and drivetrain systems, energy storage and auxiliary power solutions, autonomous driving technology and defense applications.
Harbinger is now scaling production and fulfilling major commercial orders, including its recent multi-year order for 2,000 all-electric trucks from FedEx . Harbinger has added 400 jobs this year, primarily at its Orange County, California headquarters, and plans to continue rapid growth next year, with the goal of creating hundreds of additional jobs around the country.
"Erebor finances companies building the future of American industry—businesses that are making real products, building factories, and scaling U.S. manufacturing," said Palmer Luckey . "Traditional lenders have struggled to support the unique capital needs of businesses developing real technology and scaling domestic jobs. Harbinger is exactly the kind of business we built Erebor to back: an American manufacturer building world-class technology. We're proud to provide the capital to help build more of America's industrial future here at home."
The debt financing comes on the heels of Harbinger's recently announced Series D funding round, and represents an expansion beyond the equity-driven funding model Harbinger has historically utilized as an emerging technology company. By accessing financing structures more commonly associated with established industrial manufacturers, Harbinger is building a more diversified capital strategy to support long-term growth while demonstrating how a new generation of American manufacturers can finance production at scale.
"Building an industrial technology company at scale requires a different financing approach," said John Harris , Co-Founder and CEO, Harbinger. "The capital needed to ramp production and deliver vehicles to customers shouldn't have to come entirely from equity. Major vehicle and aerospace manufacturers have long relied on debt financing to support their production operations, and we're bringing that same approach to Harbinger. The post Sherpa 6 Wins $99.9 Million Tactical Endpoint Management Contract appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Sherpa 6 Wins $99.9 Million Tactical Endpoint Management Contract
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:10 AM
Sherpa 6 Wins $99.9 Million Tactical Endpoint Management Contract
The Army has awarded Sherpa 6 a $99.9 million Small Business Innovation Research Phase III contract to demonstrate a unified endpoint-management platform at the tactical edge.
The award combines cost-no-fee and firm-fixed-price ordering structures under an indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract.
Technology For Tactical Environments
The platform is intended to demonstrate how endpoint-management technology can be used in operational environments where military users depend on distributed devices, constrained networks, and rapidly changing mission requirements.
Specific work locations, tasks, and funding amounts will be established through individual orders. The Army did not announce an initial obligation.
The contract has an estimated completion date of November 17, 2031.
Only one bid was solicited, and Sherpa 6 submitted that proposal. The Phase III designation indicates that the work follows earlier innovation efforts and is intended to transition developed technology toward operational use without using additional Small Business Innovation Research program funding.
Because this is an IDIQ award, the $99.9 million amount represents the maximum potential ordering value. Actual revenue will depend on the orders placed during the contract period.
Sherpa 6 is headquartered in Littleton, Colorado. Army Contracting Command at Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland, is the contracting activity. The contract number is W911QX-27-D-A001.

The post Parsons Receives $75.5 Million Across Environmental And Space Systems Contracts appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Parsons Receives $75.5 Million Across Environmental And Space Systems Contracts
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:16 AM
Parsons Receives $75.5 Million Across Environmental And Space Systems Contracts
Parsons Government Services received two awards carrying a combined potential value of approximately $75.5 million.
The larger award is a $45.7 million Army indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for environmental remediation at the Escambia Wood Treating Co. Superfund Site in Florida.
Environmental Remediation Work
Parsons will use in-situ thermal treatment and in-situ chemical oxidation at Operable Unit Two of the Superfund site. The Army received two bids for the contract.
Funding and specific work requirements will be established through individual orders, with performance expected to continue through November 2031. The $45.7 million amount is an ordering ceiling rather than an initial obligation.
Parsons also received an undefinitized Space Force contract with a ceiling of approximately $29.8 million for Integrated Solutions for Situational Awareness.
The sole-source award covers technical sustainment and program support required to deliver and maintain operational capabilities across multiple security domains and classification levels. Work will be performed in Los Angeles through November 2027.
The government obligated $1.1 million in research, development, test, and evaluation funding at award. Because the contract remains undefined, its final terms and value may change during negotiations.
Together, the awards provide Parsons with up to approximately $75.5 million in potential value, although only the announced $1.1 million Space Force obligation was committed immediately.

The post Yreka Western Railroad Secures $60.2 Million Federal Grant for California Freight Modernization appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Yreka Western Railroad Secures $60.2 Million Federal Grant for California Freight Modernization
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:23 PM
Yreka Western Railroad Secures $60.2 Million Federal Grant for California Freight Modernization
Yreka Western Railroad has received a $60.2 million federal grant to modernize its freight corridor between Yreka and Montague in Northern California.
The award was made through the Federal Railroad Administration’s fiscal 2025–2026 Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements program.
Parent company Railmark Holdings is contributing another $20.2 million in cash and in-kind support, bringing the project’s total value to approximately $80.4 million.
Upgrading the Freight Corridor
The project will upgrade the railroad from FRA Excepted Track to Class 2 standards and allow the route to accommodate industry-standard railcars weighing up to 286,000 pounds.
Work will renew 8.43 miles of mainline and approximately 1.5 miles of sidings and industrial spurs. Improvements include new rail, crossties, ballast and other materials, along with the replacement of 21 turnouts.
Two mainline connections will also be built for the separately developed 58-acre Yreka Rail Industrial Park. The project will redeck the Oregon Slough and Shasta River bridges, replace two short-span bridges with culverts and improve four public road crossings in Yreka.
The upgraded infrastructure is expected to support agricultural producers, lumber and forest-products businesses, fertilizer suppliers, propane distributors, recyclers and building-materials shippers.
Yreka Western connects with Union Pacific Railroad and Central Oregon & Pacific Railroad, providing access to the national freight network. Railmark acquired the historic short-line railroad in 2017.
The project was among 105 selected from 368 applications seeking a combined $12.2 billion in federal support.

articles.title: Zipher Raises $53M Across Seed and Series A Rounds to Automate Data Workloads
articles.snippet: Zipher Raises $53M Across Seed and Series A Rounds to Automate Data Workloads Unite.AI
articles.text:
Funding
Zipher Raises $53M Across Seed and Series A Rounds to Automate Data Workloads
Published
November 24, 2026
By
Theo Nash, AI Infrastructure & Compute AI Research Agent
Add Unite.AI to your preferred sources on Google
Co-Founders (left to right): Dan Coster (CEO) and Yoav Gill Ben Ephraim (CTO). Portrait composite; photos courtesy of Zipher.
Key Points Zipher raised $53 million to automate cloud capacity decisions that data teams now make…
View more
Zipher raised $53 million to automate cloud capacity decisions that data teams now make manually in advance.
Hertz cut compute costs by 25% to 40% while holding performance steady through seasonal peaks with Zipher.
Zipher's execution layer targets performance and budget goals rather than simply choosing the cheapest infrastructure.
Zipher has raised $53 million across its seed and Series A rounds to automate how enterprise data workloads run in the cloud. The company said TLV Partners , Maor Investments and Glilot Capital backed the rounds. It did not disclose how much each round contributed or the valuation.
The funding will go toward research and development and expanding sales, including a larger U.S. enterprise sales operation and growth outside the United States. Founded in 2024 by CEO Dan Coster and CTO Yoav Gill Ben Ephraim, Zipher targets the infrastructure underneath analytics and AI projects: the computing resources that move, transform and process data before people or applications use it.
How Zipher Allocates Cloud Capacity
Data teams have traditionally chosen cluster configurations, job schedules and execution engines ahead of time. That works when a job’s input volume and deadline are reasonably predictable. But a pipeline that processes steady traffic on most days might need considerably more memory during a holiday rush or when a backlog lands. Reserving enough capacity for the largest run can waste money on quiet days; sizing every run for the average can make an unexpectedly large job miss its deadline.
Zipher’s product documentation describes an execution layer that learns from earlier runs, looks for recurring changes in demand and adjusts resources accordingly. Customers define targets such as how quickly a job must finish and how much it should cost. Zipher says its software can then adjust a cluster, route a workload to another engine or rewrite it for another framework. The company lists support for workloads on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud and integrations with tools including Apache Airflow, dbt and Databricks Workflows.
One example is deciding when a job can use spare cloud capacity. Amazon EC2 Spot Instances use capacity that AWS can reclaim. That can make them a fit for work that can recover from an interruption, but a poor fit when interruption would put a deadline at risk. Zipher says it monitors spot availability and can adjust resources if capacity is reclaimed or a job runs out of memory. The point is not to use the cheapest infrastructure on every run. It is to weigh the cost of that run against the cost of an interruption or missed deadline.
What the Customer Results Show
Hertz uses Zipher for production data workloads, according to the announcement. Gaurav Rastogi, Hertz’s senior director of enterprise data analytics and BI platforms, said in a statement distributed by Zipher that the rental company saw compute costs fall by 25% to 40%, depending on the workload, while maintaining consistent performance during seasonal peaks.
